finding_key: .github/workflows/agent-iterate-ci.yml::the app token handed to the now-live iterate fixer is minted with the installation's full permission set, unlike the review-panel fixer which deliberately narrows it
evidence: Verified in the supplied files: the `Generate GitHub App token` step in .github/workflows/agent-iterate-ci.yml passes only `app-id` and `private-key` to actions/create-github-app-token@v1 — no `permission-*` inputs — so the minted token carries the installation's full repo permission set, and the following `actions/checkout` uses it without `persist-credentials: false`, leaving it in .git/config while `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and the branch's `scripts/agent/summarize-ci.mjs` run and the token is then handed to claude-code-action as `github_token`. The sibling fix job in agent-review-panel.yml does narrow the identical token to `permission-contents/pull-requests/issues: write` with the explicit rationale "this token is used in a job that checks out and executes untrusted branch code", so the inconsistency the claim describes is exactly as stated. The tie to this diff is fair: adding `allowed_bots` is what lets the agent step actually run in this job. I cannot verify which scopes the installation actually holds (agent-implement.yml only documents needing Administration:read), and if it holds checks:write the excess scope would undercut the panel's "author agent lacks checks:write" unforgeability claim — hence major rather than minor, though the underlying secret-exfiltration risk in this job is already acknowledged in the design doc's threat model.
